name: Moza
overview: Moza was a male member of the tribe of Judah, known specifically as the son of Chelubai (Caleb) by Ephah. His identity is grounded in his lineage within the tribe of Judah, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 2:46. There are no additional notes or details about his life beyond this genealogical information.
namesAndTitles: The name Moza is a proper name meaning 'sunrise.' It was not given by God but is recorded in the Scriptures to identify this individual specifically in the genealogical record of Judah.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Moza as the son of Chelubai (Caleb) and Ephah, establishing his immediate family within the tribe of Judah. No further family relationships are documented beyond this parentage.
scriptureSignificance: Moza's significance lies in his place within the genealogical lineage of Judah, underscoring the faithfulness of God's covenant people through their descendants. Though not prominent in narrative events, his mention preserves the heritage of Caleb's family line, which is important for understanding the broader biblical history of Israel.
